prompt: Why does the lesson insist on recording the model *revision* and the date checked for every product fact?

options.text: Because hardware details change between revisions (the Daisy Seed has used three different codecs) and documentation is updated, so an undated fact may no longer be true
options.explanation: Correct. Revisions change parts, and pages change. A dated, revision-specific fact can be re-checked.

options.text: It is a legal requirement for hobby projects
options.explanation: There is no such requirement; it is good engineering practice for reproducibility.

options.text: Because prices are listed by revision
options.explanation: Prices change independently of revision; this is about technical facts.

options.text: Revisions only affect the board's colour
options.explanation: Daisy Seed revisions changed the audio codec: a significant electrical change.

workedExample:
Daisy Seed datasheet v1.2.0:

| Rev | Codec |
|---|---|
| 4 | AK4556 |
| 5 | WM8731 |
| 7 | PCM3060 |

A note saying 'Daisy uses a WM8731' is only true for Rev 5. Recording revision plus date makes the claim checkable.

prompt: You plan 10 knobs. Using only the official documentation summarised in the lesson, which configuration needs an extra chip just to read knobs at all?

options.explanation: It has 12 ADC inputs, enough for 10 knobs directly.
One of them has no analogue inputs on its GPIO header.
Correct. Raspberry Pi's GPIO documentation describes the 40-pin header as 3.3 V digital inputs and outputs, with no analogue inputs, so an external ADC chip is required.

workedExample:
Count ADC inputs:

```
Daisy Seed  12 -> fits 10
Teensy 4.1  18 -> fits 10
Pi 5         0 -> needs ADC
```

That external ADC adds parts, wiring and driver work, which belongs in the cost and effort columns.

link.title: GPIO on Raspberry Pi — Raspberry Pi documentation source

prompt: Your synth must also process an external audio input (for example a filter for the Digitakt's output). Which of the three example configurations fails this must-have as specified?

options.explanation: The Seed has stereo audio inputs via its codec.
Correct. The DAC+ is output only (line out and headphones). The Codec Zero, a different Raspberry Pi audio board, adds inputs, which would be a different configuration.
The adaptor offers stereo line-in or mono mic input.
Two of the three have inputs.

workedExample:
Check the inputs row against the sources:

- Daisy Seed: audio in, 3.6 Vpp AC coupled.
- Teensy adaptor: line in or mic.
- Pi DAC+: features table lists line out and headphones only.

A must-have failure eliminates the configuration, but you can define a new one (Pi 5 + Codec Zero) and evaluate it separately.

prompt: Which statements are supported by the official sources as checked on 2026-10-16? Select all that apply.

options.text: Teensy 4.1 digital pins are not 5 V tolerant
options.explanation: Correct. PJRC: 'The pins are not 5V tolerant. Do not drive any digital pin higher than 3.3V.'

options.text: The Teensy audio adaptor works at 24-bit 96 kHz by default
options.explanation: PJRC describes the adaptor as 16-bit, 44.1 kHz.

options.text: The Daisy Seed Rev 7 codec is a PCM3060 configured in hardware mode, not over I2C
options.explanation: Correct. The datasheet's codec page says so.

options.text: The Raspberry Pi DAC+ line output is 0–2 V RMS
options.explanation: Correct. Raspberry Pi's audio documentation gives this for the DAC+ phono outputs.

workedExample:
Check each against its source:

| Claim | Source | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| T4.1 not 5 V tolerant | PJRC | True |
| Adaptor 24/96 | PJRC: 16/44.1 | False |
| Seed PCM3060 HW mode | Datasheet | True |
| DAC+ 0–2 V RMS | Pi docs | True |

Re-run this check before buying.
